title: Power torsion in the conormal module of a completed retraction
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $J\subseteq R$ an ideal, and $S$ a finite type commutative $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Suppose $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is etale over $\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus V(J)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Put $\widehat R=\varprojlim_n R/J^n$ and $\widehat S=\varprojlim_n S/J^nS$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], with the induced structural map $\widehat R\to\widehat S$. For every $\widehat R$-algebra homomorphism $\sigma:\widehat S\to\widehat R$, put $K=\ker\sigma$. There exists an integer $c\geq0$ such that $J^c(K/K^2)=0$. Here $K/K^2$ is the quotient module of the ideal $K$ by its square, with $R$-action through $R\to\widehat S$; the displayed equality means that every element of $J^c$ acts as zero on this module.

source.place: Tag 0AKJ (lemma-fully-faithful-etale-over-complement), first paragraph of existence for A=C, applying Tag 0ALQ (lemma-rig-etale), part (1), and Tag 0ALM (lemma-exact-sequence-NL) to the surjective completed retraction. Only its conormal annihilation assertion is extracted, before algebraization or henselian lifting.

proof.text: Put $B=\widehat S$ and $C=\widehat R$. Apply [lem-per-etale-away-completed-cotangent-torsion] to $(R,J,S)$. It gives a restricted-polynomial presentation of $B$, its complex $L_{B/R}^{\wedge}$, and an integer $c\geq0$ with $J^cH^0(L_{B/R}^{\wedge})=0$; it also gives completeness and finite type of $B/JB$ over $R/J$. Since $J$ is finitely generated by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] gives that $C$ is $JC$-adically complete and $C/JC\cong R/J$. This last quotient is a finite type $R/J$-algebra, generated by the empty family. Thus both $B$ and $C$ meet the complete finite-type-reduction hypotheses of the completed transitivity theorem.

proof.text: Let $i:C\to B$ be the structural map. Because $\sigma$ is a $C$-algebra map, $\sigma(i(t))=t$ for every $t\in C$. Hence $\sigma$ is surjective, with kernel $K$, and is an $R$-algebra map. It is continuous for the ideals generated by $J$: for each $n$, a sum of products of $n$ images of elements of $J$ times elements of $B$ maps into $J^nC$. Conversely the section $i$ is continuous by the same calculation. The $B$-module structure on $C$ in what follows is through $\sigma$.

source.place: Tag 0AKJ (lemma-fully-faithful-etale-over-complement), the sentence that the map is necessarily surjective

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-completed-cotangent-transitivity] to $R\to B\xrightarrow{\sigma}C$. The zero-variable presentation $\widehat{R[\varnothing]}_J=C\xrightarrow{1}C$ has zero kernel and zero differential term, so $L_{C/R}^{\wedge}$ has zero cohomology. Also, $B$ is already $JB$-adically complete, so the zero-variable presentation $\widehat{B[\varnothing]}_{JB}=B\xrightarrow{\sigma}C$ has kernel $K$ and gives $L_{C/B}^{\wedge}=(K/K^2\to0)$. The presentation independence in the cited statement permits precisely these choices. The segment $H^{-1}(L_{C/R}^{\wedge})\to H^{-1}(L_{C/B}^{\wedge})\to C\otimes_BH^0(L_{B/R}^{\wedge})$ is therefore $0\to K/K^2\xrightarrow{\partial}C\otimes_BH^0(L_{B/R}^{\wedge})$, exact at $K/K^2$. In particular $\partial$ is an injective $C$-linear map.

source.place: Tags 0ALM (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), 0AJR (equation-NL), and 0GAE (lemma-NL-up-to-homotopy), as applied in Tag 0AKJ

proof.text: Write $M=H^0(L_{B/R}^{\wedge})$. For $a\in J^c$ and a pure tensor $t\otimes m\in C\otimes_BM$, balancing gives $a(t\otimes m)=t\otimes(am)=0$ by Step 1. Pure tensors generate the tensor product by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], so $J^c(C\otimes_BM)=0$. For $x\in K/K^2$, the $C$-linearity and injectivity of $\partial$ give $\partial(ax)=a\partial(x)=0$ and therefore $ax=0$. Finally $K$ annihilates $K/K^2$ because $KK\subseteq K^2$, so its $B$-action factors through $B/K=C$. Restricting that action along $R\to B\xrightarrow{\sigma}C$ is exactly the $R$-action in the statement, since $\sigma\circ i=1$. Thus $J^c(K/K^2)=0$ with the stipulated scalar action.
